attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation has not proved that Yang-Mills reflected Wilson hairpin boundary OPEs have cycle-trivial quotient phase or positive modulus quotient on the realized Wilson cone. That is a genuine analytic boundary estimate, not a consequence of reflection positivity alone.
steps: Start with fixed collar observables F_{i,\delta}. Regulated reflection positivity gives N_{a,L,\delta}\ge0 for every finite coefficient vector c.

Use the assumed RG topology on reflected probes to pass a,L to the collar continuum limit, producing N_\delta\ge0; then take \delta\downarrow0 in entries controlled by the Wilson boundary OPE to obtain a positive collar-limit matrix N.

Represent the discrepancy between the positive collar-limit matrix and the intended same-theory target matrix by a boundary factor B: N=B\circ M, hence M=B^{[-1]}\circ N. This is the point where the proof is no longer a formal closed-cone argument.

Normalize M to unit diagonal. Pairwise positivity gives |q_{ij}|\le1, but cycle 201 showed this is incomplete because the 3 by 3 determinant also depends on the phase of q_{12}q_{23}\overline{q_{13}}.

If the quotient phase is a coboundary, conjugating by a diagonal unitary removes it without changing positivity. The remaining matrix has entries |q_{ij}|, so positivity reduces to a real modulus quotient condition on every realized finite Wilson family.

For triples, the necessary and sufficient normalized determinant condition becomes 1+2|q_{12}q_{23}q_{13}|-|q_{12}|^2-|q_{23}|^2-|q_{13}|^2\ge0 after phase removal; without phase removal the cosine term can make the determinant negative even when all 2 by 2 minors are nonnegative.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-matrix algebra is valid, but the physical input B and N have not been computed or bounded for actual continuum Yang-Mills Wilson triples near the reflection plane. In particular, the argument still assumes that additive contacts vanish and that the multiplicative anomaly representation N=B\circ M is available on the locked same-theory algebra.

assumptions: For each cutoff and collar width, the regulated Wilson OS matrix is positive: N_{a,L,delta}\ge0.
The RG/cutoff-removal topology is valid for every fixed-collar reflected Wilson probe, so N_\delta\to N entrywise for each finite family.
The boundary anomaly B has nonzero diagonal entries and represents only the multiplicative part of collar collapse after positive additive contacts have been ruled out by diagonal trace continuity.
The finite Wilson family is realized inside the locked gauge-invariant algebra; no new boundary observables are added to manufacture positivity.
The quotient phase is cycle-trivial on the realized finite family, and the remaining modulus quotient matrix is positive semidefinite.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive cutoff Schwinger forms on the locked gauge-invariant Wilson collar algebra, together with their continuum collar-limit finite OS matrices N_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\lim_{a,L}S_{a,L}(\Theta F_{i,\delta},F_{j,delta}).

target object: the intended continuum OS-positive Schwinger functions on the same gauge-invariant observable algebra after collars are removed, represented on finite families by M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j).

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated by finite reflected Wilson OS matrices and the Hadamard correction M=B^{[-1]}\circ N when boundary collar collapse has a multiplicative anomaly B.

same-theory condition: the collar-removal map may only introduce diagonal congruences or removable phase coboundaries already fixed by the observable renormalization; any non-coboundary quotient phase, negative quotient modulus minor, additive boundary contact, or algebra enlargement changes the theory rather than proving OS positivity for the intended Yang-Mills Schwinger functions.
A normalized quotient is q_{ij}=M_{ij}/\sqrt{M_{ii}M_{jj}}=(N_{ij}/B_{ij})/\sqrt{(N_{ii}/B_{ii})(N_{jj}/B_{jj})}, whenever the diagonal entries are positive.

The triangle quotient holonomy is H_{ijk}=\arg(q_{ij}q_{jk}\overline{q_{ik}}); it vanishes modulo 2\pi for all triples exactly when the finite quotient phase can be removed by a diagonal unitary congruence on that connected component.

equations.label: collar OS positivity
equations.valid_when: Reflection positivity holds at the regulated level and fixed-collar reflected Wilson probes converge entrywise in the RG topology.

equations.label: same-theory Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: The only collar-collapse discrepancy between the collar limit and the intended observable is a nonzero multiplicative boundary Gram factor B on the same finite Wilson family.

equations.label: three-point determinant obstruction
equations.valid_when: \widehat M is the 3 by 3 diagonal-normalized intended OS matrix with unit diagonal and q_{ij}=\widehat M_{ij}; positivity requires this determinant and all principal minors to be nonnegative.

equations.label: phase coboundary criterion
equations.valid_when: All q_{ij} are nonzero on a connected finite family; zero entries are treated componentwise by restricting to the nonzero support graph.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a realized Wilson triple with all pairwise inequalities valid but with H_{123}\ne0 and determinant of B^{[-1]}\circ N negative, or find a realized finite family whose quotient phase is removable but whose quotient modulus matrix has a negative principal minor.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma refines the previous finite Schur-preimage criterion into two separately testable obligations: phase coboundary control and modulus quotient positivity. It is a bridge lemma because it identifies exactly what extra boundary data must be controlled for the closed-cone collar argument to imply OS positivity for the same continuum theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let N(F) be the collar-limit OS matrix for a finite locked Wilson family F and let B(F) be the multiplicative boundary Gram anomaly produced by reflected collar collapse, with nonzero entries. The intended same-theory OS matrix is M(F)=B(F)^{[-1]}\circ N(F). A sufficient finite-matrix bridge is: after normalizing diagonals, the quotient phase of Q_{ij}=N_{ij}/B_{ij} is a coboundary and the quotient modulus matrix |Q| is positive semidefinite on every realized family. Then M(F) is positive, so collar reflection positivity transfers to the intended OS form. Conversely, a nontrivial triangle quotient phase or a modulus quotient with a negative principal minor is a concrete falsifier of the bridge.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if actual Wilson boundary OPE data shows unavoidable non-coboundary quotient holonomy or negative modulus quotient minors on realized triples, because then the RG-to-OS route cannot prove same-theory positivity without changing the observable algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one can prove, on a dense locked Wilson core, that quotient phases are cycle-trivial and all modulus quotient matrices are positive semidefinite after additive contacts vanish; this would turn the collar closed-cone result into a valid OS positivity passage.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still producing new structure: cycle 202 turned the phase-sensitive determinant warning into a two-part bridge lemma with concrete finite tests. This is more actionable than another closed-cone restatement and keeps the work focused on the Wilson boundary OPE obstruction.

dependency_updates.description: The formal closed-cone passage remains valid only up to the collar-limit matrix N. The same-theory target requires the finite Schur-preimage condition M=B^{[-1]}\circ N, now decomposed into quotient phase coboundary plus modulus quotient positivity.
The locked algebra must realize enough Wilson triples to test quotient holonomy and determinant obstructions; pairwise Wilson probes are insufficient.
The topology must converge mixed reflected Wilson products and their boundary OPE anomaly data, not merely individual loop expectations.

falsifiers: A three-hairpin Wilson family with pairwise |q_{ij}|\le1 but H_{123}\ne0 large enough that det(B^{[-1]}\circ N)<0 is a phase falsifier of same-theory OS positivity.
A finite Wilson family with cycle-trivial quotient phase but a negative principal minor of the modulus quotient matrix |B^{[-1]}\circ N| falsifies the modulus half of the bridge.
A nonzero additive boundary contact with zero diagonal would contradict the positive-contact vanishing argument; if such a contact appears, the assumed boundary OPE positivity is invalid.

A collar limit that requires adding boundary Wilson observables, changing loop renormalization at t=0, or quotienting by a new boundary Hilbert sector fails the same-theory condition even if the modified matrix remains positive.
If the RG convergence topology controls ordinary Wilson loops but not mixed reflected products \Theta F_i\,F_j, then the closed-cone passage is not valid for the OS quadratic forms actually needed.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 202 learned that the next bridge is not just finite Schur-preimage positivity in one block. It decomposes into a phase problem and a modulus problem. The phase problem is cohomological on each finite Wilson support graph: zero triangle holonomy makes the quotient phases removable by diagonal unitary congruence, while a nonzero triangle holonomy is the first phase falsifier. After that removal, the remaining obstruction is a real positive-semidefinite modulus quotient. This gives a sharper and more operational Yang-Mills target: compute the reflected Wilson boundary OPE for triples, extract quotient holonomy and modulus minors, and test whether the intended same-theory OS matrix is positive.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute a symbolic 3 by 3 reflected Wilson hairpin model: parameterize B_{ij}=r^B_{ij}e^{i\phi^B_{ij}} and N_{ij}=r^N_{ij}e^{i\phi^N_{ij}}, form q_{ij}=N_{ij}/B_{ij}, and search for a realized-looking regime where every 2 by 2 minor is nonnegative but the triangle determinant is negative. Then map each parameter to a boundary OPE coefficient that Yang-Mills estimates would need to bound or eliminate.
